title: EU Data Act, Article 5(3): DMA gatekeepers excluded as eligible third parties

answers.name: Exclusion of designated gatekeepers from receiving connected-product data (Data Act Art. 5(3))
answers.description: Undertakings designated as gatekeepers under the Digital Markets Act are not eligible third parties: users cannot have product data shared with them, and third parties may not pass the data on to them.
answers.sector: Data-based aftermarket and related services; data processing services (W/120 1.B, CPC 84) – classification contested

notes.nt_lfv: The criterion is formally origin-neutral, but almost all designated gatekeepers are headquartered outside the EU: a de facto national-treatment argument.
notes.nt_like: Assumed for the analysis: gatekeepers and other data-service providers compete for the same data-based services. Contested; this is the pivotal question.
notes.mfn_differential: Whether the effect falls disproportionately on suppliers of some non-EU Members (e.g. the United States) rather than others needs evidence.
notes.x_paragraph: Contestability and fairness of digital markets are not Article XIV grounds. A (c) argument would need the measure to secure compliance with GATS-consistent laws.
notes._scenario: Illustrative inputs for research discussion, based on Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 as adopted. Amendments to the Data Act have since been proposed (Digital Omnibus); check the current text. Schedule entries are assumed and must be verified against the EU's consolidated GATS schedule.
